stories.h: Sofia Coppola revisits Marie Antoinette at 20
stories.why: Auteur deep-dive plus a new streaming doc
sum: Letterboxd talks to Sofia Coppola as Marie Antoinette returns in a 4K restoration and joins the Criterion Collection on 10 November. Alongside it comes Making Marie Antoinette, a documentary cut from nearly 100 hours of on-set footage shot by her late mother Eleanor Coppola, finished by Sofia and narrated with Eleanor's journal entries read by Diane Lane. It streams on MUBI from 6 November.

Coppola reflects on the film being booed at Cannes and panned mostly by male critics, its later rebirth as a cult favourite (including on TikTok), the post-punk soundtrack, the pastel Versailles look and that stray pair of Converse. She also hints she wants her next project to feel more hopeful.
pts: Making Marie Antoinette streams on MUBI from 6 Nov
4K restoration and Criterion release on 10 Nov
Long read: reception, music, Priscilla and what's next

stories.h: Letterboxd's November 'Unreleased Gems' shelf
sum: Letterboxd Video Store has picked four festival films with no other release for this month's Unreleased Gems shelf, available to rent for 30 days from 12 November to 12 December. They are Crash Land, a comedy about small-town Canadian amateur stuntmen making a tribute film after a friend dies, starring Finn Wolfhard and Gabriel LaBelle; The Only Way Out Is Through, about three estranged friends reuniting in the Rockies; The Plan, a Slamdance single-take thriller about activists in a Los Angeles flat; and Mouth Full of Golds, a Tribeca documentary on the rise and fall of grillz in hip-hop.
Availability varies by country (mostly US, UK, Nordics, Australia and New Zealand), and prices differ per title.
pts: Four festival titles, rentable 12 Nov to 12 Dec
Includes a Finn Wolfhard comedy and a grillz documentary
Region-locked; check availability in Indonesia

stories.h: Wild Horse Nine and 20 great buddy comedies
stories.why: New McDonagh plus a ready-made watchlist
sum: Pegged to Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine, which opens in US cinemas on 8 November via Searchlight, Letterboxd rounds up twenty buddy comedies. The new film pairs John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as two CIA operatives who, after setting up a coup in Chile, head to Easter Island for a break, where their regrets and paranoia come out amid constant bickering.

The list runs from McDonagh's own In Bruges and The Banshees of Inisherin to Planes, Trains & Automobiles, Hot Fuzz, The Nice Guys, The Sting, Daisies and Sholay. Note that the piece is sponsored by the film.
pts: McDonagh reunites with Sam Rockwell, opposite John Malkovich
US release 8 Nov
Sponsored list, but a solid watchlist

stories.h: North Macedonian satire wins Tokyo's top prize
stories.why: Asian festival winners to watch for
sum: The Tokyo International Film Festival gave its top prize to Milcho Manchevski's Sister Brother Manhole Cover, a darkly comic look at North Macedonia's wealth divide. Sun Xun's mixed-technique Chinese animation Magic Atlas won the special jury prize, Lisandro Alonso was named best director for Double Freedom, and the acting awards went to Hu Ling for The Night That Binds Us and Ryo Narita for Two Cigarettes, Three Nights.

Heysel 85 took the audience award. In the Asian Future strand, Ariani Darmawan's Jani Be Good earned a special mention. Rolf de Heer led the competition jury, and Kurosawa Akira Awards went to Mipo O and Mohammad Rasoulof.
pts: Top prize: Sister Brother Manhole Cover
Best director: Lisandro Alonso
Special mention for Ariani Darmawan's Jani Be Good

stories.h: Gugu's World: Brazil's tender Oscar entry
sum: Allan Deberton's Gugu's World, a double winner in Berlin's Generation Kplus section and Brazil's Oscar submission, follows 11-year-old Gugu, a queer boy and gifted footballer in the north-east backlands who loves colour, make-up and music. He lives with his spirited grandmother, who is developing dementia, while his remarried father struggles to accept who he is.

Screen Daily calls it a touching, compassionate coming-of-age drama, praising Yuri Gomes's lead performance, Teca Pereira as the grandmother and the vivid production design. The sunny first half gives way to a more melancholy second half, and the film leans into sentiment. It opened in Brazil on 5 November.
pts: Berlin Crystal Bear winner; Brazil's Oscar pick
Standout child lead in Yuri Gomes
Warm but sentimental

stories.h: Kefi: a strange, bold Japanese grief comedy
sum: Kisin Saito's debut Kefi, which premiered in Tokyo's Nippon Cinema Now strand, brings three estranged sisters back to the family home after their divorced father dies. It is told in four segments set on the same day and narrated by the father's ghost, and it swings between mourning and surreal, darkly funny detours.

Screen Daily finds it eye-catching and divisive. The striking switches between colour and black-and-white, the Japanese indie soundtrack and the confident direction all impress, but the story often stops making sense and the overlapping perspectives can feel impenetrable. It is pitched at festivals and art-house buyers looking for something unusual.
pts: Debut feature, shot by the director himself
Four interlocking segments on one day
Visually daring, narratively baffling

stories.h: Sony Classics buys Jeunet's Violette, incl. SE Asia
stories.why: Amélie director's next is headed your way
sum: Sony Pictures Classics has bought rights for the US, Latin America and Southeast Asia to Jean-Pierre Jeunet's Violette in a deal with Studiocanal. It is the company's fourth Jeunet film, after Amélie, The City of Lost Children and Micmacs.

Adapted from Valérie Perrin's novel Fresh Water for Flowers and co-written with Guillaume Laurant, the film follows a cemetery caretaker whose quiet life is upended when a stranger arrives, forcing her to face her past. Leïla Bekhti, Matthias Schoenaerts and Melvil Poupaud star. No release date has been announced.
pts: Rights include Southeast Asia
Jeunet reunites with Amélie co-writer Laurant
Leïla Bekhti and Matthias Schoenaerts star

stories.h: Banderas to captain Cohn and Duprat's Mare Nostrum
stories.why: Sharp satirists take on a big moral drama
sum: Antonio Banderas will star in Mare Nostrum, the next drama from Argentina's Mariano Cohn and Gastón Duprat, the duo behind Official Competition, in which Banderas also starred. He plays the captain of a huge container ship carrying a billion-euro cargo from Istanbul to Cape Town who comes across a sinking boat of African migrants during a storm. His decision to take them aboard triggers an international political crisis.
The directors call it their most ambitious film yet, mixing tension and dark humour. HanWay Films is launching sales at AFM, and shooting starts in Spain in March 2027.
pts: Banderas reunites with the Official Competition directors
Migrant-rescue drama set at sea
Shoot begins March 2027 in Spain

stories.h: Italy passes major film and TV law overhaul
sum: Italy's Senate passed a sweeping film and TV reform 123 to 0. It creates a new Cinema and Audiovisual Agency from 2028 to run funding schemes, an industry forum and a project assessment commission. It also promises simpler shooting permits and easier co-production rules to attract foreign shoots, priority for first and second features and independents, support for genre films, money to reopen cinemas, and consent rules for AI use of performers' work.

Tax credit rates (currently 40%) and overall funding stay the same for now, with follow-up laws due within two years. Industry reaction is mixed, with authors and producers questioning the new agency's independence.
pts: New national film agency from 2028
Tax credits unchanged for now
AI consent rules for performers

stories.h: daine trades cloud-rap for indie sleaze on a sharp debut
stories.why: Indie rock with an emo edge
sum: The Line of Best Fit gives daine's studio debut, In Endless Awe & Agony (out 6 November), an 8/10. daine moves away from the emo cloud-rap of earlier releases toward glitchy indie rock, mixing electroclash, electro-pop, twee and Midwest emo, sometimes within a single song. The review compares it to early Modern Baseball and 2016-era Grimes.

Unlike indie-sleaze revivalists who sing about parties and drugs, daine writes about lost identity, consumerism, privilege and a generation unsure of its future. The reviewer singles out "Supervillain" as the record's moral centre, plus "PQC", "White Collar" and "I Used To Kill" with aldn. The verdict: a jaded record that still refuses to look away.
pts: 8/10 from The Line of Best Fit
Indie rock meets electroclash and emo
Out 6 November

stories.h: bar italia's drummer goes deep and hazy as Eterna
stories.why: For fans of bar italia and slowcore
sum: Eterna is Guillem Peeters, the Barcelona-born, London-based multi-instrumentalist who drummed on bar italia's Tracey Denim. His third album, Push (out 6 November), gets an 8/10 from The Line of Best Fit. The scrappy lo-fi collage of his first two records gives way to slow, careful post-rock that the review compares to Talk Talk, Bark Psychosis and David Pajo's guitar playing, with touches of trip-hop, slowcore and dub.

The reviewer's point is that Peeters has stopped trying to look cool and now clearly cares about the craft. Picks include the slow build of "Kyrie", the shimmering "Shadowcasting for the Villain", the trip-hop "Gum" and the pastoral closer "Rex". The review calls it a major step forward in a single year.
pts: 8/10 from The Line of Best Fit
Hazy post-rock and slowcore
Out 6 November

stories.h: Yoo Doo Right push krautrock somewhere new
sum: Montréal experimental rock band Yoo Doo Right, who are named after a Can song, return with their fourth LP, Build and Rest by the Shepherd's Light. Drummer John Talbot and multi-instrumentalist Justin Cober build on Neu! and Can grooves, then add doom-laden post-rock in the vein of Godspeed You! Black Emperor, shoegaze haze and drone. Jessica Moss plays violin.

The Line of Best Fit gives it 7/10, praising the band for avoiding rote imitation. The long instrumentals "Two Hoarders" and "Tortue" stand out, but the reviewer's pick is the fierce post-punk turn of "Doldrums, Doldrums, Eviler Than The Devil". Some uneven shifts and drifting ambient passages hold the record back.
pts: 7/10 from The Line of Best Fit
Krautrock meets post-rock and shoegaze
Out 6 November
stories.q: Yoo Doo Right Build and Rest by the Shepherd's Light

stories.h: Toro y Moi announces new album Unusua
stories.why: Indie favourite with a new record
sum: Chaz Bear will release a new Toro y Moi album, Unusua, on 20 November through his own label, Company Studio. The announcement came with a new single, "Motive". It follows "Proof", which came out a couple of weeks earlier.

Bear played, arranged and produced the seven-track record himself at Scenic Route in Berkeley and 2200 Studios in Sausalito. The tracklist is "Keynote", "Motive", "Proof", "Poor Connection", "Interval", "Lull" and "Obsolete". No tour dates have been announced yet.
pts: Unusua is out 20 November
New single "Motive" out now
Self-produced, 7 tracks

stories.h: Liquid Mike share fuzzy power-pop single "Inanimate Object"
sum: Power-pop band Liquid Mike have released "Inanimate Object". It is their second new song of the year, after "Drowning Machine" in May, and follows Hell Is An Airport, which came out a little over a year ago.

Stereogum describes it as a catchy, fuzzed-out rave-up that is quietly about what happens after death. Bob Sweeney directed the video. The band is currently on tour with Oso Oso. No new album has been announced yet.
pts: New single plus video
Follows May's "Drowning Machine"
On tour with Oso Oso

stories.h: AMI Awards 2026: Reality Club wins Best Alternative Album
sum: The 29th Anugerah Musik Indonesia took place on 4 November at Ciputra Artpreneur in South Jakarta, with 67 categories. Tulus won the most awards (four, including Best Male Solo Pop Artist and production for "Teh Hijau"). Idgitaf won three, including Best Album for Berusaha di Bawah Hujan, and no na won Best New Artist.

In the alternative categories, Reality Club took Best Alternative Album for Who Knows Where Life Will Take You?, Kunto Aji won best solo alternative artist for "Berani", and Dongker with Jason Ranti won best alternative duo or group for "Disarankan Di Bandung". Black Horses won Best Rock Album and Burgerkill took the metal award. Bernadya and Perunggu also won.
pts: Tulus 4 wins, Idgitaf 3
Reality Club: Best Alternative Album
Dongker and Jason Ranti also won
stories.q: Reality Club Who Knows Where Life Will Take You?

stories.h: Lafa Pratomo, Jason Ranti and Isyana tackle AI anxiety
sum: Producer Lafa Pratomo has teamed up with Jason Ranti and Isyana Sarasvati on "Dogs Are Always True", an electro-pop-backed rap track about fears around AI and the noise of online life. It came out on 3 November as the fifth single from the EP Garis Tegak, a series that pairs musicians with contrasting styles.

The idea started with Jason Ranti's story of a neighbour who lost their job to AI. The three wrote the song in loose jam sessions with nothing prepared. Isyana says the internet gives people freedom but asks them to be careful about what they believe. It is Lafa's first release of his own after about a decade producing for others.
pts: Fifth single from EP Garis Tegak
Inspired by a job lost to AI
Lyric video on KithLabo YouTube
stories.q: Lafa Pratomo Jason Ranti Isyana Sarasvati Dogs Are Always True

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: HOKA x Marni Clifton 11 lands in three bold colours
stories.why: Colourful, playful runner from a whimsical label
sum: Marni and HOKA have teamed up again, this time on the Clifton 11, HOKA's everyday cushioned trainer. The upper is engineered mesh, and Marni adds raised 3D silicone lines along the side, a textured knit collar lining, small metal details near the toe and a plaid insole.

It comes in three colours: near-tonal black with red lace loops, a vivid orange upper on a white sole with a silver band, and a clean white with silver trim. Every pair includes two extra sets of speckled or striped two-tone laces. It costs $275 and launches on 12 November through Marni, then reaches HOKA and other stores on 13 November.
pts: $275, Marni launch 12 Nov, wider release 13 Nov
Black, bright orange or white
Two extra sets of two-tone laces in the box

stories.h: Chopova Lowena opens its Clubhouse with Violet Grohl
sum: The London label Chopova Lowena has a new campaign called Clubhouse, starring Violet Grohl and shot by Grace Difford. It celebrates the brand's first shop, which opened in August on Teesdale Street in East London.

An exclusive merch line features Petal, the brand's club mascot, on striped tees, camo bandanas, caps, socks, boyshorts and stickers. In the shop, a Skirt Bar lets you design your own version of the brand's signature pleated skirt from deadstock, vintage Bulgarian and new fabrics. The pieces are sold in the store and online, and the article lists no prices.
pts: Petal mascot merch: tees, caps, bandanas
Design-your-own skirt bar in East London
Mix of folklore, sportswear and subculture

stories.h: Space Jam Tune Squad Crocs drop 9 November
sum: Crocs is putting the Space Jam Tune Squad on its Classic Clog. The clog is white with red and blue trim around the opening and heel strap, based on the team's uniforms from the film's big game.
A large Tune Squad logo charm covers most of the toe, and the original Space Jam logos are printed on the footbeds. It comes in adult and kids' sizes for $70 and goes on sale at Crocs on 9 November.
pts: $70, 9 Nov on crocs.com
White with red and blue trim
Oversized Tune Squad toe charm

stories.h: Whitaker Group's pink and purple New Balance 2010s
stories.why: Soft colour pops on a casual runner
sum: The Whitaker Group and New Balance have released a two-pair 2010 pack called Willful Bias For Identity. One pair has a cream mesh base with earthy pink suede, and the other is grey mesh with purple suede. Both have frayed suede, visible stitching, raw edges and an orange N logo.

It is the next chapter in the Willful Bias series and draws on personal heritage. Antiisoulcial and Nuku shot the campaign, with florals and a community restaurant counter. Each pair costs $155 and went on sale on 5 November at New Balance and The Whitaker Group, with a raffle at A Ma Maniére.
pts: $155 per pair, out 5 Nov
Pink-on-cream and purple-on-grey suede
Deconstructed, raw-edge details

stories.h: The Moomins move into Bottega Veneta's woven bags
sum: Bottega Veneta's new Moomin collection hides the references to Tove Jansson's stories in the craft rather than printing them on top. The Small Andiamo bag weaves red and white leather like Moominmamma's striped apron, wallets use the blue and red of Moominhouse, and the Small Cabat has Comet in Moominland cover art inside the pouch.

There are also hand-woven leather charms of Moomintroll, Moominmamma and Moominhouse, a pencil holder, and a crocheted leather Snufkin figure that takes artisans several days to make. The collection launches in Japan only: at an Isetan Shinjuku pop-up on 11 November, then at Japanese stores and online from 18 November. The article lists no prices.
pts: Japan only: 11 Nov pop-up, 18 Nov wider
Moomintroll and Moominhouse bag charms
Story details hidden in weaves and linings

stories.h: Barbour and FARM Rio go tropical a third time
sum: Barbour and the Brazilian label FARM Rio have released their third collection together, mixing British country outerwear with FARM Rio's bright prints. FARM Rio redesigned Barbour's tartan two ways: one in classic brown and blue, and one tropical version with bold florals and banana motifs.

The range is led by showerproof jackets, quilted styles, reversible liners and overshirts, alongside knitwear, skirts, dresses and accessories. Inside, there are floral linings and logos from both brands. It is on sale now on the Barbour and FARM Rio websites, and the article lists no prices.
pts: Out now online
Banana-print tartan
Waxed and quilted jackets with floral linings

stories.h: This week's 8 drops: Supreme x Vaquera, adidas x BAPE
stories.why: One-stop list of this week's streetwear drops
sum: Hypebeast's weekly drop guide starts with Supreme x Vaquera, which includes hoodies, collage tees, jeans and a duvet set. It went on sale on 5 November and arrives in Asia on 7 November. adidas x BAPE follows on 7 November with a late-'90s basketball range, including the Crazy Energy+ sneaker and a reversible shark hoodie.

Also on the list are a Palace x Burberry capsule sold only at Palace's new London store, a green and yellow Crenshaw Skate Club x Sprite line (global release 9 November, $50 to $120), a Pas Normal Studios x Salomon trail-running kit, and new pieces from Fear of God, Kith x TUMI, and The North Face x Cecilie Bahnsen.
pts: Supreme x Vaquera reaches Asia 7 Nov
adidas x BAPE basketball drop 7 Nov
Crenshaw Skate Club x Sprite from 9 Nov

stories.h: Lagos Fashion Week street style is all bold colour
sum: Dazed's photo story from Lagos Fashion Week SS27 shows a crowd going all in on bright colours, strong contrasts and statement shapes, while still looking relaxed and easy. Standout looks included crimson overshirts with gold brooches and chartreuse slip dresses with gold bangles.
On the runway, Orange Culture came back to Lagos after several seasons showing in Berlin. Fruché showed sculpted wooden bodices, and IAMISIGO showed tall shapes woven from natural fibres.
pts: Crimson and chartreuse lead the palette
Orange Culture returns to Lagos
Relaxed styling with bold colours

stories.h: Margiela x Gentle Monster's crushed, mismatched shades
stories.why: Odd, arty eyewear for a niche taste
sum: Maison Margiela and the Korean eyewear brand Gentle Monster revealed their fourth collaboration at a warehouse show in Seoul. The collection has 68 styles, 43 sunglasses and 25 optical frames, built around Margiela's idea of deconstruction.

Some frames are made from mismatched parts that look stitched together, some have swooping, uneven edges, and others look crushed, with split metal and lenses popping out. At the show, a plaster curtain was smashed to reveal dancers moving like broken dolls next to a white grand piano. The article gives no prices or release details.
pts: 68 styles: 43 sunglasses, 25 optical frames
Mismatched and crushed-looking frames
Fourth collab since 2023

stories.h: Coperni shuts down after eight years
sum: The Paris label Coperni is closing. Founders Arnaud Vaillant and Sébastien Meyer confirmed the news after talks broke down with Tomorrow, the brand's distributor and a shareholder, over unpaid money and licensing terms. Tomorrow had ended its licensing deal, and Coperni sought court protection in Paris earlier this year.

The founders tried to buy back the brand but could not resolve disputes over control and money, and the cancelled Fall/Winter 2026 show added to the strain. They say they are proud of what they built and have more ideas to share later.
pts: Main French company is closing
Licensing dispute with Tomorrow
Fall/Winter 2026 show was cancelled

stories.h: Activists confront RSPO over fires on member plantations
stories.why: Palm oil, land and corporate impunity
sum: Walhi, TuK Indonesia and allied groups protested on 3 November outside the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil's annual conference in PIK 2, Tangerang, accusing the certifier of greenwashing while member concessions burned. Security pushed the protesters back. Walhi counted 1,467 high-confidence hotspots inside 65 RSPO-member concessions; Satya Bumi estimated about 3,750 hectares burned across 110 member companies. Haze has been linked to over 400,000 respiratory infection cases, per the Health Ministry.

Police have named 245 people and 20 companies as fire suspects, and the Environment Ministry has sealed 57 companies. RSPO says only 0.8% of the 1.9 million hectares burned lies in member concessions, but admits signs of unusual burning and is reviewing some sites.
pts: Groups filed complaints with Nestlé, Unilever, PepsiCo and P&G over supplier links
Geopix: 88% of hotspots in certified Kalimantan concessions were in orangutan habitat
RSPO denies evidence that members burned land deliberately

stories.h: Nickel boom leaves Sulawesi women poorer and sicker
sum: A Climate Rights International report, featured by Mongabay, draws on interviews with 40 women near nickel mining and smelting sites in Southeast and Central Sulawesi. They describe red, polluted seas, shrinking fish catches, undrinkable water, skin and respiratory illness, and token dust compensation. One Bajo midwife can no longer perform a newborn sea ritual because the water is fouled.

Women have protested, sued and organized, but face exclusion from village decisions, no free prior and informed consent, and risk of criminalization. CRI urges the government to stop permitting new captive coal plants for nickel, and EV makers to press suppliers. Komnas HAM's chair warned the industry risks violating rights.
pts: Economist estimates over 95% of Morowali's industrial value leaves the region
Walhi: only about 30% of nickel output goes to EV batteries
Komnas HAM flags risks of criminalization and violence against women

stories.h: West Sumatra village rejects toll road through ancestral land
sum: Residents of Nagari Pandai Sikek in Tanah Datar, West Sumatra, are opposing a planned route of the Padang–Pekanbaru toll road, a National Strategic Project, that would cut through farmland, homes, songket weaving workshops and communal pusako land inherited through the female line. Community estimates say 18 hectares of farms and seven songket businesses would be hit.

Customary leaders say they back the toll but reject this route, and have told district, provincial and national governments. Walhi West Sumatra supports them, citing constitutional and agrarian rights. The deputy regent calls the project beneficial; Hutama Karya apologized for earlier survey disruption and promised further public consultation.
pts: Weavers and farmers fear compensation can't replace their livelihoods
Pusako land is held through matrilineal inheritance
Next public consultation still pending

stories.h: Pre-dawn armed police raid on girls' pesantren draws criticism
sum: A legal column in Konde.co examines a police raid on Pondok Pesantren Hamalatul Quran in Sukoharjo, Central Java. Officers reportedly arrived around 3:20 am with long-barreled weapons to investigate arson and threats against a food stall. Twelve girls aged 10 to 16 and four teachers were reportedly taken for questioning and released after guardians pressed police.

Author Tutut Tarida of the gender-justice advocates' collective argues that legality alone isn't enough: the new criminal procedure code limits search scope, and child-protection law requires putting children's interests first. She calls for review of the chain of command, trauma-informed support for the girls, and mandatory gender and age risk assessments in police operations.
pts: Children taken in simply for being present, the column says
Cites new KUHAP limits on searches and seizures
Urges independent oversight and remedies for those affected

stories.h: Israel demolishes five buildings in Biddu, displacing 100+
sum: Israeli forces demolished five residential buildings, 12 apartments in all, in Biddu northwest of Jerusalem on Thursday, displacing more than 100 people, Middle East Eye reports. Residents say troops gave no warning, fired stun grenades and tear gas, and stopped them retrieving belongings. The army cited missing permits in Area C, where Palestinians are almost never granted them.

The owner believes it was retaliation linked to his son, a prisoner freed in last year's exchange and deported to Egypt. A council member said two homes had no court demolition order. The PA's Jerusalem governorate called it a dangerous escalation and has logged 471 demolition operations from January to October.
pts: Area C permits are almost never granted to Palestinians
Some homes had pending legal challenges, council says
471 demolition operations recorded Jan–Oct 2026

stories.h: Gaza: child killed in Bureij; 1,134 children lost limbs
sum: Israeli attacks killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday, including a child shot in the Bureij refugee camp, Democracy Now! reported, citing Al Jazeera, despite the ceasefire.

The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor says 1,134 children in Gaza have lost limbs since 2023, and that Israeli travel restrictions keep hundreds from specialized care abroad. It says Israel is blocking equipment and specialist teams needed to make prosthetics inside Gaza, where only eight certified prosthetics professionals remain, and warned that growing children without adjusted limbs face lasting pain and disability.
pts: At least four killed Thursday, per reports
Euro-Med: 1,134 child amputees since 2023
Only eight certified prosthetists left in Gaza

stories.h: Trump vows to end Israel aid; Providence votes to divest
stories.why: Arms to Israel and BDS wins
sum: Mondoweiss's Michael Arria argues Trump's Election Day claim that US military aid to Israel will end this year shouldn't be taken at face value: Congress has already appropriated billions through 2028, and the plan reportedly swaps grants for arms sales and deeper US-Israeli military integration via the next defense bill. Trump tied the move to criticism from Abdul El-Sayed.

Separately, Providence, Rhode Island, became the largest US city to divest from Israel after voters passed Question 7, backed by incoming democratic-socialist mayor David Morales. An exit poll found 74% of voters called the Iran war a major factor.
pts: Billions already appropriated through 2028
Ex-State official warns integration gives Israel leverage
Providence divestment is a ballot-box win for the movement

stories.h: Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim elected to US Senate
sum: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed beat Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's Senate seat and will be the first Muslim senator in US history, sworn in on 3 January, Al Jazeera reports. He survived anti-Muslim attacks led by Trump, who called him a jihadist without evidence, and more than $30 million spent against him by AIPAC in the primary.

El-Sayed, who has accused Israel of genocide in Gaza, ran on public healthcare, affordability and moving war spending home. Turnout was high in majority-Arab Dearborn, and he did well with Black voters in Detroit. Analysts called the result a rejection of anti-Muslim politics; the win helps Democrats retake the Senate.
pts: Beat AIPAC spending and Islamophobic attacks
Openly pro-Palestine platform
Dearborn turnout surged after the smears

stories.h: Record number of hijabi women win US offices
sum: The US midterms elected a record five hijab-wearing Muslim women to statewide and national office, Middle East Eye reports, all progressive Democrats: Ruwa Romman to Georgia's state senate, Palestinian immigrant Aber Kawas in New York, Nabeela Syed in Illinois, Maryam Khan in Connecticut, and Ilhan Omar re-elected to Congress for a fifth term.

The wins came amid a wave of anti-Muslim rhetoric from Republicans, and for Omar, a recent federal raid on her home and reported efforts to strip her citizenship, which she denies. A Muslim advocacy group argued Islamophobia backfired, pointing to Omar's larger margin.
pts: Four state senators-elect plus one congresswoman
Kawas's father was deported after post-9/11 detention
Omar re-elected despite federal pressure
